questions.scenario: A container named products uses /category as its partition key. The application knows both the id and the category of the product that it needs.
questions.question: Which Python SDK call retrieves the product with the lowest Request Unit (RU) charge?

options.text: container.query_items(query="SELECT * FROM c WHERE c.id = @id", parameters=[...], enable_cross_partition_query=True)
options.why: A cross-partition query costs more RUs than a direct lookup and searches every partition.

options.text: container.read_all_items() followed by a filter in Python
options.why: Reading every item consumes RUs for the whole container.

options.text: container.read_item(item=product_id, partition_key=category)
options.why: Correct. A point read by id and partition key goes directly to the item and is the cheapest read operation.

options.text: container.query_items(query="SELECT * FROM c WHERE c.id = @id", parameters=[...], partition_key=category)
options.why: This query stays in one partition, but a query still costs more than a point read for the same item.

questions.explanation: A point read with read_item, using the id and the partition key value, is the most efficient way to fetch a single item.

questions.question: A Python application connects to Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL by using CosmosClient and DefaultAzureCredential. The developer has the Owner role on the Cosmos DB account, but every request to read items returns 403 Forbidden. What should you do?

options.text: Assign the Cosmos DB Built-in Data Contributor role to the developer's identity on the account by using a Cosmos DB SQL role assignment
options.why: Correct. Microsoft Entra ID data access uses Cosmos DB data plane role assignments, which Azure control plane roles such as Owner do not grant.

options.text: Assign the Contributor role on the resource group
options.why: Contributor is a control plane role and does not grant data plane access to items.

options.text: Change the default consistency level to Strong
options.why: Consistency levels do not affect authorization.

options.text: Enable the analytical store on the container
options.why: The analytical store is for analytics workloads and does not affect authorization.

questions.explanation: Cosmos DB has its own data plane RBAC. Assign a data plane role such as Cosmos DB Built-in Data Contributor or Cosmos DB Built-in Data Reader.

questions.question: A web API passes a category value entered by a user to a Cosmos DB query. You must prevent query injection. What should you do?

options.text: Build the query string by using an f-string and escape single quotes
options.why: Manual escaping is error-prone and still treats user input as part of the query text.

options.text: Use a parameterized query such as WHERE c.category = @cat and pass the value in the parameters argument
options.why: Correct. Parameters keep user input separate from the query text.

options.text: Set enable_cross_partition_query to False
options.why: This setting controls partition routing and has no effect on injection.

options.text: Disable the indexing policy on the container
options.why: Indexing does not affect query injection and disabling it makes queries more expensive.

questions.explanation: Parameterized queries pass values separately from the query text, which prevents injection.

questions.question: You are investigating the cost of operations in a Python application that uses the azure-cosmos SDK. Which TWO statements are true?

options.text: The RU charge of the most recent operation can be read from the x-ms-request-charge response header
options.why: Correct. Every response includes this header with the RU charge.

options.text: A query that does not filter on the partition key and is not scoped to one partition key value runs as a cross-partition query
options.why: Correct. Without a partition key the query must run against every physical partition, which increases the RU charge.

options.text: A new CosmosClient instance should be created for every request to reduce RU charges
options.why: Creating clients repeatedly adds latency and wastes resources. A single client should be reused for the lifetime of the application.

options.text: upsert_item always fails if an item with the same id and partition key exists
options.why: upsert_item replaces an existing item. create_item is the method that fails when the item exists.

questions.explanation: Monitor x-ms-request-charge and scope queries to a partition key to control RU consumption.

questions.question: You are designing a container for chat sessions. Most requests read or write the messages of one session, and there will be millions of sessions. Which partition key should you choose?

options.text: /messageType, which has three possible values
options.why: Three values give very low cardinality and create hot partitions.

options.text: /createdDate, set to the current date
options.why: All of today's writes would go to one logical partition, which creates a hot partition.

options.text: /region, which has five possible values
options.why: Five values give low cardinality, and most requests are not scoped by region.

options.text: /sessionId
options.why: Correct. sessionId has high cardinality and matches the main access pattern, so most requests stay in one partition.

questions.explanation: A good partition key has many distinct values, spreads writes evenly, and appears in the filters of most requests.
